items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: how would Ernest Hemingway write this liner notes or album review? Well it’s going to be pretty dry.

ctx.x: Well I’m trying to think every time you sit down to write a review and are you aware of using a particular phrase multiple times? How do you keep your writing fresh from one session to the next?

Very interesting. The writing aspect for me is frankly the easier part. That’s number one. I really like — when I’m doing, let’s say it’s an album review or nowadays a single review. Okay? I have a process that I like to use, which is not only repetitive repetitive listenings, that’s number one. I read the liners. When I do the listenings I also, if I’m able to I’ll alternate the tracks. Okay? And I do that because sometimes there’s a sequence in the production. All right? Which is an art in and of itself from…

another savant, all right? Without a doubt. And when Glenn plays, especially when he plays with that Harmon mute, he really gets almost that Miles Davis buzz. Okay? Which is, actually it’s an aspect of physics, all right? The vibrations and the pitch, you know, have to be just right for that Harmon mute to really zing. And he is gifted here, with his ear, where he knows that he wants to get that Miles Davis type buzz sound from Miles’ earliest days, you know from the Prestige Recordings, “If I Were a Bell” and…
